text:
alex: quick data drop — ran a 2h sweep on rtx-pool comparing microbatch size mb=4 vs mb=12 for chatstream + non-streaming completions. results: p95 (chatstream) mb=4 = 130ms, mb=12 = 220ms; p99 mb=4 = 310ms, mb=12 = 560ms. throughput (tokens/s) +2.3x at mb=12. KV cache hit-rate fell ~12% at mb=12 (seen as kvcache evictions).

maria: do you have the kernel selection logs? wondering if we flipped into a slower kernel path for streaming when batching grew.

alex: yeah — attaching quick profile snippet: 
```
profile summary: mb=4 -> kernel=fast-attn-v2 (hot path), avg kernel latency 3.2ms/token
mb=12 -> kernel changed to fallback-gemm (matmul generic) for ~18% of tokens, avg kernel latency 6.8ms/token
kvcache: hit 88% (mb=4) vs 76% (mb=12)
queueing: head-of-queue wait increased ~40ms for streaming requests at mb=12
```
link to flamegraph: https://perf.redwood/internal/flame/2798765432

priya: this matches what we saw in staging — streaming workflows are much more sensitive to tail because they flush partial tokens and emit early. larger mb groups improve avg throughput but you pay with higher headwait + stale KV profiles. p99 spike seems dominated by kv-miss path + kernel fallback.

dave: for non-streaming (completions) mb=12 looks fine — p99 is still within SLA and unit cost drops. For chatstream we should cap mb to <=6 to keep p99 under SLO. Could we do dynamic mb sizing: route.streaming ? mb=4-6 : mb=12 and add kv-hit feedback to bump down mb when kvcache drops?
sam: another subtlety: kernel chooser currently picks fast-attn when batch*seq > threshold. For chatstream seq is small but kv spill increases effective seq during KV replay which triggers a different kernel path (we saw fallback to generic matmul). small code snippet from chooser logs: 
```
if (batch*seq >= 1024) choose fast-attn-v2
else if (kv_spill) choose fallback-gemm
```
That kv_spill branch is being hit more often at higher mb because eviction pressure and interleaving requests.

ci-bot: canary run summary (2h): streaming route mb=10 -> observed +2% p95, +18% p99, kv-hit -10%. rollback recommended if we can't mitigate kernel fallback.

maria: proposed action items: 1) short-term: implement per-route mb cap (streaming default = 4, allow override). 2) medium: feedback loop — measure per-10s kv-hit and reduce mb if hit < 80%. 3) investigate kernel chooser: add check for kv_spill frequency so we don't trigger fallback-gemm on ephemeral evictions. 4) perf test: 24h canary with k/v instrumentation and token-level traces.

alex: agreed. i'll open PR for per-route cap + metric exporter for kv-hit. @dave can you prototype the mb feedback heuristic? @priya can you run extended 24h canary after PR? I'll add a dashboard for quick rollback triggers (p99 > baseline * 1.3 or kv-hit drop > 8%).

priya: noted — will schedule canary after PR merge. also we should capture per-token kernel histograms in traces so we can separate kernel tail vs queue tail.

dave: will prototype heuristic: if (streaming) mb = min(config.max_stream_mb, max(2, floor( current_kv_hit * config.base_mb ))) — simple for canary.

sam: one more thought — consider prefix caching for chat so kvcache eviction pressure is lower for long-lived conversations; that might let us raise mb safely for power users.

alex: TL;DR: mb tradeoff = throughput vs tail. chatstream needs conservative mb and kv-aware heuristics; completions can be more aggressive. action owners assigned. :thumbsup:
